notes.text: The author states that condition d) makes the indicated ordered topological-space structure satisfy condition c) of the Scholie, referring to p.27. The next three case paragraphs describe the written s_ij as fibrants propres, describe boundaries of the Sigma_i in the nonsingular case, and give a fibration/boundary description in the combined case. These are reports of the manuscript, not independent theorem statements or verified conclusions.

The marginal note asks for the Sigma_ij to be manifolds with boundary and gives the boundary as the union of the written Sigma_kij and Sigma_ikj. It then says c’est sans doute une conséquence de la condition précédente. That qualification is the author’s own. The note begins with the literal de = shorthand and ends with two points and a dash; neither feature is expanded or normalised in the page text.

Section13 is headed Une digression. The author returns to the Sigma/product setting without a given I, introduces the displayed topological-category data, and states a preorder claim for pi_0 of the object space under the written fibrancy supposition. The image of the displayed pi_0 map is proposed as the relation’s graph. The last lower expression repeats the single pi_0 of a product; that literal repetition is retained instead of H’s product of two pi_0 expressions. Reading these statements was not a proof check.

The authorial number29 is at the head; pale foliation66 at the foot is in another hand. Reference27 and section13 are written numerals. Twenty-one main text/display baselines are counted, including the second cancelled line and lower target expression, with slanted margin and interlinear writing inventoried separately. No expected mathematical formula was used to replace a source or target index.

M0611 is resolved to the visibly dotted and descending target j. M0612, M0613 and M0614 remain undecided. M0613 is narrowed to cpl.|compl. because the initial c is visible. M0614 retains both the uncertain overwritten 0/Sigma layer and the uncertainty of lowered versus baseline placement. The tentative cancelled filtré preserves visible f/i/l and final-accent evidence while leaving its middle uncertain.

The first insertion leader supplies the apparent parenthesis before satisfait; no extra text parenthesis is retained. The initial d of d’espace and the first Sigma_i subscript are reworked but have no independently recovered old letter. A detached upper bar in the first product’s final Sigma is consistent with a pen lift in a four-stroke Sigma; the same construction occurs in the final lower Sigma on this sheet. Its local overline alternative remains explicit for later notation review.

The two dark points under the definition connector and the thin broken stroke at the right paper edge are reproduced without assigning linguistic or mathematical meaning. Their provenance is uncertain. The last vertical marker is drawn from its wavy/reworked left component and straight right upright; the horizontal shaft retains its middle thickening, whose possible history as an earlier head remains unassigned.

Individual audit rectangles follow the saved crop locations for each insertion, cancellation, marginal passage, numeral, lexical disagreement, doubtful formula and uncertain drawn trace. Position comments identify clipped neighbouring strokes without attaching them to the audited phrase. The separate point above the clear comma after topologiques has uncertain provenance and punctuation attachment; comma leads the retained comma/semicolon alternatives.

A compact irregular dark fleck in the blank interval below the case paragraphs was inspected in crop p24_isolated, source box [625,1225,730,1310]. Its dark core has a gray halo, with no recoverable connected letter or stroke sequence. It is recorded as an excluded unassigned surface fleck of uncertain origin, without adding a linguistic token or manuscript figure.
